resolution_comment_excerpts: @josham : Given that you have a `NaN` in `value_y`, it would be impossible to have `Int64` (would be a floating dtype actually). That being said, uncertain as to why you're getting `object` though... cc @jreback
I agree that this should be able to return Int types here; this was just put in place in 0.24 so may not be well handled for empty types

@jreback I came across another merge issue with Int64. I can add to this issue or create another, let me know what you prefer. ```python x = pd.DataFrame({ 'date': [pd.Timestamp('2018-01-01')], 'value': pd.Series([np.nan], dtype='Int64') }) y = pd.DataFrame({ 'date': [pd.Timestamp('2018-01-01')], 'value': pd.Series([4], dtype='Int64') }) z = x.merge(y, on=['date']) ``` ```python Traceback (most recent call last): File "scratch.py", line 23, in <module> z = x.merge(y, on=['date']) File "/python/lib/python3.6/site-packages/pandas/core/frame.py", line 6868, in merge copy=copy, indicator=indicator

@jreback, @TomAugspurger the following seems to fix both issues. Does this seem correct to you? ``` --- a/pandas/core/internals/concat.py +++ b/pandas/core/internals/concat.py @@ -190,6 +190,8 @@ class JoinUnit(object): pass elif getattr(self.block, 'is_sparse', False): pass + elif getattr(self.block, 'is_extension', False): + pass else: missing_arr = np.empty(self.shape, dtype=empty_dtype) missing_arr.fill(fill_value) ```
